summary_paragraph: A man with a history of CAD, CABG, COPD, esophagitis, and alcohol abuse was admitted for chest pain that occurred while attempting to eat spinach, which he felt stuck in his throat, followed by vomiting and chest pressure. Initial evaluation ruled out acute cardiac ischemia with normal troponins and non-diagnostic EKG changes. A CT abdomen showed no acute surgical process but noted a stable moderate-to-severe SMA stenosis and a hiatal hernia. An EGD revealed severe esophageal ulceration and a 9 mm stricture at the gastroesophageal junction, which was dilated to 12 mm. His chest pain was attributed to esophageal pathology rather than cardiac causes. He was managed with acid suppression, including a switch from omeprazole to sublingual lansoprazole for better compliance, and a soft diet. He remained stable, with no arrhythmias or respiratory deterioration, and was discharged home with plans for outpatient EGD follow-up and continued medication management.
